candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall establish and enforce specific limits to implement the provisions of 40 CFR Parts 403.5(a) and (b), as required by 40 CFR Part 403.5(c).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and which locally developed limits under 40 CFR 403.5 are enforceable numeric discharge limits for pretreatment/indirect dischargers affects which limits Purpose A must compare against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Such BMPs shall be considered local limits and Pretreatment Standards.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating BMPs as local limits and pretreatment standards could change which parameters have enforceable numeric limits versus non-numeric management practices for Purpose A applicability.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall, within sixty (60) days of the effective date of this permit, (1) submit a WRITTEN CERTIFICATION that a technical evaluation has been demonstrated that the existing technically based local limits (TBLL) are based on current state water quality standards and are adequate to prevent pass through of pollutants, inhibition of or interference with the treatment facility, worker health and safety problems, and sludge contamination, OR (2) submit a WRITTEN NOTIFICATION that a technical evaluation revising the current TBLL and a draft sewer use ordinance which incorporates such revisions will be submitted within 12 months of the effective date of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This creates a time-bound monitoring/evaluation and submittal obligation whose satisfaction in FY2025 must be determined for Purpose B, and the certification-vs-notification branch affects what compliance evidence is required.

candidates.exact_span: All specific prohibitions or limits developed under this requirement are deemed to be conditions of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether locally developed prohibitions or limits are incorporated as permit conditions determines if they are enforceable limits Purpose A must apply to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The specific prohibitions set out in 40 CFR Part 403.5(b) shall be enforced by the permittee unless modified under this provision.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation of 40 CFR 403.5(b) prohibitions as enforceable permit conditions, subject to modification, affects which numeric or categorical limits Purpose A must evaluate and whether modifications displace the default prohibitions.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall analyze the treatment facility influent and effluent for the presence of the toxic pollutants listed in 40 CFR 122 Appendix D (NPDES Application Testing Requirements) Table II at least once/year
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a minimum annual monitoring frequency for Table II pollutants on both influent and effluent, which Purpose B must evaluate for applicability and whether required monitoring occurred in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: and the toxic pollutants in Table III at least once/3 months.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes quarterly monitoring frequency for Table III pollutants, affecting whether Purpose B finds monitoring was required and whether evidence shows it was performed at the required interval.

candidates.exact_span: If, based upon information available to the permittee, there is reason to suspect the presence of any toxic or hazardous pollutant listed in Table V, or any other pollutant, known or suspected to adversely affect treatment plant operation, receiving water quality, or solids disposal procedures, analysis for those pollutants shall be performed at least once/3 months on both the influent and the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional monitoring trigger depends on interpretive judgments about suspicion and available information; different readings change whether quarterly monitoring was required (Purpose B) and how missing results for those pollutants should be classified when evidence of the trigger is absent or ambiguous (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The influent and effluent samples collected shall be composite samples consisting of at least 12 aliquots collected at approximately equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period and composited according to flow.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sampling design requirements affect whether collected data satisfy the permit monitoring obligation (Purpose B) and whether absent or nonconforming samples count as adequate evidence versus unresolved missing-evidence cases (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Sampling and analytical procedures shall be in accordance with guidelines established in 40 CFR 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reference to 40 CFR 136 methods ties monitoring validity to federal analytical requirements; interpretation of conformance affects whether monitoring was properly performed (Purpose B) and whether reported or missing results are usable evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The effluent samples shall be analyzed to a level at least as low as required in (6) below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required analytical detection/reporting level for effluent samples, cross-referenced to item (6), affects the effective numeric comparison threshold Purpose A must use when determining whether measurements exceed applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: Where composite samples are inappropriate, due to sampling, holding time, or analytical constraints, at least 4 grab samples, taken at equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period, shall be taken.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The grab-sample alternative is conditional on appropriateness constraints; different interpretations of when composites are inappropriate change whether the required monitoring protocol was met (Purpose B) and whether missing data reflect non-required sampling or inadequate evidence (Purpose C).
